fix(android): raise the keyboard on every Reply

## Summary

Follow-up to #1793, from review: choosing **Reply** on the post that is already quoted did not raise the keyboard. The composer's focus effect was keyed on `session.replying`, and that value does not change when the same post is chosen again.

The fix replaces the screen's local counter and `LaunchedEffect` with a `replyRequests` counter on `ChannelSession`, bumped by a new `reply(post)`, and passes it as the composer's `focusRequest`. The net change is about the same size; the effect that missed the case is gone.

## Test
- `ChannelTest.aReplyQuotesItsPostIsSentAndComesBackAfterAFailure` now replies to the same post twice and expects two requests.
- No visual change.

Refs #1784

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

[Bug] Document the bash prompt cursor bug fixed upstream in 5.3 patch 20

## Linked issue

Closes #584

- [x] This issue exists and a maintainer **agreed it** before this PR was opened — in a comment, or by ticking the **Maintainer agreement** box on their own issue.
- [x] The issue is **labelled** — exactly one type (`bug` / `enhancement` / `tweak` / `documentation`) and at least one `area:*` — and its title reads `[Type] Summary`. See [Labelling](../CONTRIBUTING.md#labelling).
- [x] **This PR carries its own labels and milestone**, mirroring the issue(s) it closes — `gh pr create` inherits neither, and a PR with no milestone never appears on the board a maintainer merges from.

## Intent (what & why, in human terms)

On Linux, a bash terminal whose panel gets wider (a move to a wider dock slot, or a new terminal whose panel widens after the prompt is drawn) can leave the cursor a few columns short of the end of a coloured prompt, and typing then overwrites the prompt (#584).

The fault is in bash's bundled readline, not throng. Before bash 5.3 patch 20, readline recomputes a wrapped prompt's invisible-character layout only when the screen gets narrower, so after a widen its cursor arithmetic is off by the invisible bytes on the old last line. Upstream fixed it in [`bash53-020`](https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/bash/bash-5.3-patches/bash53-020). Ubuntu 26.04 ships `5.3-2ubuntu1` (patch 9), and no Ubuntu or Debian series carries the fix yet; getting it into Ubuntu is [Launchpad bug 2173620](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/2173620).

There is nothing for throng to change, so this PR documents the behaviour and the recovery.

## Outcomes (what changed, in human terms)

`docs/linux.md` → *Terminals* gains one entry: which bash versions are affected, what the user sees, that pressing Enter recovers, and the Launchpad link.

How the cause was established:

- Captured bash's own output through a real pty: after an 80 → 150 column widen with a wrapped colour prompt, its redraw ends with five backspaces, one per invisible byte on the old last line. A colourless prompt and a narrowing resize redraw correctly.
- Reproduced in throng with a one-worker throwaway E2E: moving a bash terminal from a 38-column slot to an 80-column one left the cursor at column 48 instead of 53.
- In an `ubuntu:26.04` container, under `LANG=C.UTF-8`: the installed package and an unpatched rebuild of its source are both 5 columns short, and the same source with the `bash53-020` hunk applied is correct. Three runs, identical results; under `LANG=C` none of the three misplaces the cursor.

The probes were temporary and are not part of this PR.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(opencode-v2): show a failed compaction as failed

Code changes: +43 -0\
Tests: +167 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

A failed OpenCode 2 compaction now shows as failed, with OpenCode's own error, instead of "The conversation history was compacted".

## Why

Fixes #7863

OpenCode ends a failed compaction with a normal `end_turn` and reports the failure only in `session_info_update`. AO judged the result from the turn state, so it showed success and set `compactedAt` when nothing had been compacted.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Failed compaction shows "The conversation history was compacted" | Shows "The agent ran into a problem" with "Compaction summary did not match the required template" |
| Failed compaction is saved as a `completed` turn and sets `compactedAt` | Saved as a `failed` turn with OpenCode's error; `compactedAt` stays empty |
| A compaction that fails with a prompt error is saved as `failed`, but its turn is left out of the timeline, so nothing appears | The error appears in the timeline |
| Successful compaction shows "The conversation history was compacted" | Unchanged |

## How

- `client.go` reads `_meta["opencode/compaction"]` during a compaction turn. The latest status wins. The same status on a normal turn is ignored, so a failed automatic compaction doesn't fail the user's turn.
- `conversation.go` fails the turn from that status instead of settling it as compacted.
- A compaction turn has no prompt or reply, and the timeline only includes turns with an item on the page. A failed one also emits `ChatEventError`, so it can be seen. The app already hides that row when it repeats the turn's error, so the message shows once.
- Retry stays hidden because there's no human prompt to resend. Running `/compact` again is the retry.

The status is read in the shared ACP driver, next to the existing JetBrains session-failure metadata. Only OpenCode sends this key.

## Testing

**Real desktop app** with OpenCode 2.2.5 and a scripted fake model. The failure was forced by having the model reply without OpenCode's summary template. OpenCode was placed at AO's private installer path by hand.

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `/compact` fails | Error shown once, no Retry, `compactedAt` empty |
| Reload the failed session | Error still shown |
| Send a message after the failure | Agent replies normally |
| `/compact` succeeds | Compacted row shown, `compactedAt` set |

**New tests**, confirmed failing before the fix: reported failure with and without a message, a failure not carrying into the next compaction, a prompt error reaching the timeline, and a failed status on a normal turn.

**Local CI on macOS**
- `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass. `golangci-lint` v2.13.2 passes on the ACP driver package, not the whole repo.
- On the rebased commit, with `-race`: `chatdriver/acp`, `chatdriver/nativeacp`, `chatdriver/opencodeacp`, `service/chat` and `storage/sqlite/store` pass.
- The full `go test -race ./...` ran before the rebase, and 6 tests failed in packages this PR doesn't change. All 6 also fail on clean `main` on this Mac:
  - `TestPrepareSessionHomeAnchorsConditionalIncludeHeaders`
  - `TestCrushLocalAuthStatusDoesNotUseProviderCatalog`
  - `TestV2RejectsFailuresWithoutSideEffects`
  - `TestWrongOpenCodeMajorIsRejectedBeforeACPProcessLaunch`
  - `TestCueCommandPreservesNativeEvalEOFAndOptionBehavior`
  - `TestRuntimeIntegrationSupervisedExitKeepsInteractiveShell` (intermittent: 7 of 8 runs failed on `main`, 6 of 8 on this branch)

**Not run:** the Linux and Windows jobs, a real provider failure, a real automatic compaction, and other ACP agents.

fix: take the beta draft id from the create response

## Summary

```text
Create draft prerelease
- list releases and filter for the new draft tag
+ POST /releases and keep the id from that response
Upload and verify assets
  gh release upload
- gh api releases/$RELEASE_ID/assets | sort
+ require a numeric RELEASE_ID
+ write the asset listing, then sort it
  diff local SHA-256 against uploaded digests
```

The Beta publish job created draft `v0.2.1-beta.1`, then looked it up by listing releases. A draft has no git tag yet, that lookup returned nothing, and `RELEASE_ID` stayed empty. Upload still succeeded. Verification then called `releases//assets`, the 404 body was sorted into the digest file because the API call was in a pipeline, and `diff` failed. Cleanup was skipped, so the draft stayed unpublished.

## Evidence

- **Before:** [Publish beta](https://github.com/alimek/t3-factory/actions/runs/42362035434/job/128374372517) failed at "Upload and verify assets" with `RELEASE_ID` empty and `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`. The six assets were already on draft `437492043` and their SHA-256 digests matched the job's local hashes.
  **After:** That draft is published as prerelease [v0.2.1-beta.1](https://github.com/alimek/t3-factory/releases/tag/v0.2.1-beta.1), target `814032b5e7807b3987aedcb75bd571c95158c4b9`. Latest remains [v0.2.0](https://github.com/alimek/t3-factory/releases/tag/v0.2.0). `pnpm check` passed locally. The next Beta run is the first execution of the new create path.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The workflow change reverts cleanly. The published prerelease does not: `v*` tags cannot be updated or deleted.

**Blast Radius:** beta channel

Only the Beta publish job changes. Stable releases are untouched. No documentation change: a failed attempt still deletes its own draft, and a published beta is still a prerelease that is never marked latest. No migration. No new test: this is workflow shell, not a behavior the test suite can reach.
